Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- Dozens of Defense Department personnel are actively engaged in fighting the wildfires raging in Southern California, Pentagon officials said Tuesday, and thousands more National Guard and active-duty military personnel are available to help. The Rice fire, east of Camp Pendleton, caused the evacuation of the Fallbrook community. Paul McHale, assistant secretary of defense for homeland defense, said that 12 Defense Department firefighting teams, with 12 engines, are already working the blazes and more than 17,000 National Guardsmen are potentially available if needed. In addition, he said, 550 Marines from Camp Pendleton are preparing to deploy to the fire area. "All of the aid that we provide is the result of a request ... from the state," McHale said. "However, we have been very proactive in independently preparing those capabilities for the possibility of such requests, and we have reached out early to state officials." California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger has already called up 1,500 National Guard troops, including more than 200 taken from border duty to help with supplies and security at San Diego's Qualcomm Stadium and DelMar Fairgrounds and Racetrack, where thousands of evacuated residents are taking shelter. Schwarzenegger also requested and received from the federal government six "modular airborne fire fighting systems" units -- which are C-130s that drop water and fire suppressant on the blazes.  Watch California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger talk about the crisis » . The Pentagon provided 11 helicopters equipped with water buckets to fight the fires, McHale said. Aerial attacks on the fires, however, have been minimal because of high Santa Ana winds with gusts approaching 70 mph. In an effort to make room for more civilians who have had to evacuate their homes, sailors stationed in Southern California are abandoning their barracks. "Orders have been given to all sailors ashore in barracks to move to shipboard billeting to provide room for evacuees," said a Tuesday statement released by the U.S. military. Only essential personnel are requested to report to duty at Naval Base San Diego, Naval Amphibious Base in Coronado, and Naval Air Station in El Centro. Those bases have also set up cots and tents for evacuees. Also, the Navy has offered an Aegis cruiser, a guided missile destroyer, and two fast frigates to support evacuation efforts. Meanwhile, the Pentagon designated March Air Reserve Base as the primary staging area for medical and relief supplies coordinated by the Federal Emergency Management Agency, McHale said. And some 100 California National Guard medical personnel are helping alleviate "critical staffing shortfalls" at the San Diego Veterans Center, whose hospital staff are under voluntary and mandatory evacuation orders. The fires are also having a direct effect on military personnel -- McHale said 1,400 Navy personnel and their families have been forced to evacuate, and Camp Pendleton ordered 3,000 Marines to evacuate because of the fire, the Pentagon announced Tuesday evening. In all, the military has about Video 20 facilities around the San Diego area.  E-mail to a friend .

outputs.L1:
**(CNN) —** Dozens of Defense Department personnel are actively fighting the wildfires raging across Southern California, Pentagon officials said Tuesday, while thousands more National Guard and active-duty military personnel remain available to assist.

The Rice Fire, east of Camp Pendleton, prompted the evacuation of the Fallbrook community.

Paul McHale, assistant secretary of defense for homeland defense, said 12 Defense Department firefighting teams, equipped with 12 engines, were already battling the blazes and that more than 17,000 National Guardsmen could be made available if needed. In addition, 550 Marines from Camp Pendleton were preparing to deploy to the affected area.

“All of the aid that we provide is the result of a request ... from the state,” McHale said. “However, we have been very proactive in independently preparing those capabilities for the possibility of such requests, and we have reached out early to state officials.”

California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger has already activated 1,500 National Guard troops, including more than 200 reassigned from border duty to assist with supplies and security at San Diego’s Qualcomm Stadium and the Del Mar Fairgrounds and Racetrack, where thousands of evacuated residents are sheltering.

Schwarzenegger also requested and received six “modular airborne firefighting systems” from the federal government. The units are C-130 aircraft that drop water and fire suppressant on the blazes.

The Pentagon also provided 11 helicopters equipped with water buckets to combat the fires, McHale said. However, aerial firefighting efforts have been limited by powerful Santa Ana winds, with gusts approaching 70 mph.

To make room for more civilians forced to evacuate their homes, sailors stationed in Southern California are vacating their barracks.

“Orders have been given to all sailors ashore in barracks to move to shipboard billeting to provide room for evacuees,” the U.S. military said in a statement released Tuesday.

Only essential personnel have been asked to report for duty at Naval Base San Diego, Naval Amphibious Base in Coronado, and Naval Air Station El Centro. Those installations have also set up cots and tents for evacuees.

The Navy has also offered an Aegis cruiser, a guided-missile destroyer, and two fast frigates to support evacuation efforts.

Meanwhile, the Pentagon designated March Air Reserve Base as the primary staging area for medical and relief supplies coordinated by the Federal Emergency Management Agency, McHale said.

About 100 California National Guard medical personnel are also helping alleviate “critical staffing shortfalls” at the San Diego Veterans Center, where hospital staff are subject to voluntary and mandatory evacuation orders.

The fires are also directly affecting military personnel. McHale said 1,400 Navy personnel and their families had been forced to evacuate. Camp Pendleton also ordered 3,000 Marines to evacuate because of the fire, the Pentagon announced Tuesday evening.

In total, the military has about 20 facilities in the San Diego area.
outputs.L2:
Pentagon officials said Tuesday that dozens of Department of Defense employees were directly involved in battling the Southern California wildfires, while thousands of additional National Guard members and active-duty troops stood ready to assist.

The Rice Fire, burning east of Camp Pendleton, forced residents of Fallbrook to evacuate. According to Paul McHale, assistant secretary of defense for homeland defense, 12 Defense Department firefighting crews and 12 fire engines were already working against the flames. More than 17,000 National Guard troops could also be made available if necessary, and 550 Marines from Camp Pendleton were preparing to deploy to the affected area.

McHale explained that Defense Department assistance is provided in response to requests from the state. However, he said the Pentagon had acted in advance to prepare resources for possible requests and had contacted state officials early.

California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger had already activated 1,500 National Guard troops. That number included more than 200 personnel reassigned from border duty to help distribute supplies and provide security at San Diego’s Qualcomm Stadium and the Del Mar Fairgrounds and Racetrack, where thousands of evacuees had sought shelter.

At Schwarzenegger’s request, the federal government also supplied six Modular Airborne Fire Fighting System units—C-130 aircraft capable of dropping water and fire retardant. McHale said the Pentagon additionally provided 11 helicopters fitted with water buckets. However, aerial firefighting operations were limited because strong Santa Ana winds were producing gusts close to 70 mph.

To create additional space for civilians displaced from their homes, sailors based in Southern California were ordered to leave their barracks. A U.S. military statement issued Tuesday said all sailors living ashore in barracks had been directed to move into accommodations aboard ships so the vacated rooms could be used by evacuees.

Only personnel performing essential duties were asked to report to Naval Base San Diego, Naval Amphibious Base Coronado, and Naval Air Station El Centro. Those installations also prepared tents and cots for displaced residents.

The Navy offered several ships to assist with evacuation operations: an Aegis cruiser, a guided-missile destroyer, and two fast frigates.

McHale also said the Pentagon selected March Air Reserve Base as the main staging location for medical equipment and relief supplies coordinated by the Federal Emergency Management Agency. About 100 medical personnel from the California National Guard were helping address critical staff shortages at the San Diego Veterans Center, where hospital employees were subject to both voluntary and mandatory evacuation orders.

Military members were themselves directly affected by the fires. McHale said 1,400 Navy personnel and their families had been evacuated. On Tuesday evening, the Pentagon also announced that Camp Pendleton had ordered 3,000 Marines to leave because of the fire.

Altogether, the military operates approximately 20 facilities in the San Diego area.
outputs.L3:
Dozens of Department of Defense personnel and 12 military firefighting teams were mobilized to help battle the wildfires spreading across Southern California. Thousands of additional military personnel remained on standby and could be deployed if state and local authorities requested further assistance.

Near Camp Pendleton, the Rice fire forced the evacuation of the community of Fallbrook. In response, approximately 550 Marines prepared to deploy to the affected area to support firefighting and emergency-relief efforts.

California also activated 1,500 National Guard troops. They were assigned to help distribute supplies and provide security at evacuation shelters, including large emergency centers established at Qualcomm Stadium and the Del Mar Fairgrounds.

The federal government supplied six C-130 aircraft equipped for airborne firefighting, along with 11 helicopters capable of dropping buckets of water. However, powerful Santa Ana winds created dangerous flying conditions and severely restricted aerial firefighting operations.

To make more shelter space available for displaced civilians, sailors stationed in Southern California were ordered to leave their barracks temporarily and move aboard ships. The vacated military housing could then be used to accommodate people forced from their homes by the fires.
outputs.L4:
Southern California wildfires forced residents from their homes and triggered a broad, coordinated response involving local, state, and federal agencies. The Defense Department mobilized firefighting teams, National Guard troops, Marines, aircraft, and helicopters to support efforts to contain the blazes and protect threatened communities. Military housing was also made available to accommodate some residents displaced by the fires.

Dozens of military personnel were already working alongside civilian firefighters, while thousands of additional service members remained available if conditions worsened or authorities requested more assistance. The military’s role included providing personnel, equipment, transportation, logistical support, and potential aerial firefighting capabilities.

However, powerful Santa Ana winds created exceptionally dangerous conditions. Strong gusts accelerated the spread of the fires, carried embers into new areas, and made it difficult for crews to establish containment lines. The winds also sharply restricted the use of aircraft and helicopters, limiting water and fire-retardant drops at a time when aerial support was urgently needed.

The response demonstrated the scale of federal resources available to assist Southern California, but it also highlighted the challenges facing firefighters. Even with substantial military support and thousands of personnel on standby, extreme winds and rapidly changing fire conditions continued to complicate containment and evacuation efforts.
